limits: Tiny fixed-clock two-host data fits configured DBengine caches; warm API evidence only.
Client request overlap does not establish simultaneous Rust evaluators.
RSS is the whole Agent; high-water includes startup and earlier qualification.
Wire duration includes connection establishment, server work and final body delivery; excludes client decoding/validation.
HTTP sample counts are logical and do not count fetched pages or allocated bytes.
Shared host; no CPU/frequency isolation, cold-disk, high-cardinality, IoT or physical ARM performance claim.
All528 complete generated pairs preserve row-array order; selected707 builtin originals are unordered for instant rows and do not establish that physical order independently.
Workspace peak increases range0–1240bytes across the generated pairs; binary text grows768/304bytes in release/release-min. No new raw arrays or persistent Step fields.
Eight release and21release-min medians are slower; largest observed median increases6.6/5.7percent. Small timing changes on this shared host have no established causal attribution.

Live before/current cohorts ran at different times; generic timings use seven alternating measured pairs after one warmup pair. Neither is CPU/frequency isolated, saturation throughput or physical ARM performance.
Whole-process RSS/high-water includes startup/prior qualification and excludes kernel page cache/backing size. It is not Rust-only or total system query RAM.
Server statistics precede final C output commit and omit its completed assembly/compression. Wire duration includes connection/request/final-byte read.
The two-point generic diagnostic and tiny warm two-host/one-tier live fixture do not establish cold-disk, high-cardinality, IoT or large-parent scaling.
Historical complete language/foreign/interface cohorts keep their actual earlier source identities; this change adds no language feature, ABI, provider, storage, reference, dependency or cap policy.
